# Lab 12.14: TabularFM Model

## What We Are Going to Do
Predict with the pre-trained TabFM foundation model through `AI.PREDICT` (Preview), with no training, and compare it with a trained model.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Regression with no training.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">WITH prepared AS (
  SELECT *, RAND() &lt;= 0.8 AS is_train
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ml_datasets.penguins`
  WHERE body_mass_g IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT body_mass_g, predicted_body_mass_g
FROM AI.PREDICT(
  (SELECT * EXCEPT (is_train) FROM prepared WHERE is_train),
  (SELECT * EXCEPT (is_train) FROM prepared WHERE NOT is_train),
  label_col =&gt; 'body_mass_g')
LIMIT 10;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The first query is the "context" (examples with labels); the second is what to predict.

2. **[SQL] Classification.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">WITH prepared AS (
  SELECT *, RAND() &lt;= 0.8 AS is_train
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ml_datasets.penguins`
  WHERE sex IS NOT NULL AND sex != '.'
)
SELECT sex, predicted_sex, predicted_sex_probs
FROM AI.PREDICT(
  (SELECT * EXCEPT (is_train) FROM prepared WHERE is_train),
  (SELECT * EXCEPT (is_train) FROM prepared WHERE NOT is_train),
  label_col =&gt; 'sex')
LIMIT 10;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Measure accuracy.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">WITH prepared AS (
  SELECT *, MOD(ABS(FARM_FINGERPRINT(CONCAT(island, CAST(culmen_length_mm AS STRING), CAST(body_mass_g AS STRING)))), 5) != 0 AS is_train
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ml_datasets.penguins`
  WHERE sex IS NOT NULL AND sex != '.'
)
SELECT ROUND(COUNTIF(sex = predicted_sex) / COUNT(*), 3) AS tabfm_accuracy
FROM AI.PREDICT(
  (SELECT * EXCEPT (is_train) FROM prepared WHERE is_train),
  (SELECT * EXCEPT (is_train) FROM prepared WHERE NOT is_train),
  label_col =&gt; 'sex');</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   This uses a fixed (hash-based) split. Train a `LOGISTIC_REG` model on the same `is_train` rows and compare its accuracy on the other rows.

4. **[Console] Check pricing.** TabFM uses token-based pricing from late October 2026, on top of normal query cost. Look at the job's details for the TabFM usage.

5. **[CLI] Run a TabFM regression from bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
"SELECT body_mass_g, predicted_body_mass_g FROM AI.PREDICT(
  (SELECT * FROM \`bigquery-public-data.ml_datasets.penguins\` WHERE body_mass_g IS NOT NULL AND MOD(CAST(body_mass_g AS INT64), 5) != 0),
  (SELECT * FROM \`bigquery-public-data.ml_datasets.penguins\` WHERE body_mass_g IS NOT NULL AND MOD(CAST(body_mass_g AS INT64), 5) = 0),
  label_col =&gt; 'body_mass_g') LIMIT 5"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>
